title_en: Gansu Province Agricultural Reclamation General Corporation v. Agricultural Bank of China, Aksai Kazak Autonomous County Sub-branch — appeal of dispute over loan contract guarantee

full_text_en:
Gansu Provincial Agricultural Reclamation General Company

v.

Aksai Kazak Autonomous County Sub-branch of Agricultural Bank of China

— dispute over guaranty for loan contract (appeal)

Fa Gong Bu [2000] No. 2

Supreme People's Court of the People's Republic of China

Civil Judgment

(1999) Jing Zhong Zi No. 347

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Gansu Provincial Agricultural Reclamation General Company. Domicile: No. 185 Yanchang Road, Chengguan District, Lanzhou City, Gansu Province.

Legal Representative: Wang Yinding, Manager of the Company.

Agent ad litem: Zhao Qinghua, lawyer of Gansu Xiehe Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Dai Rui, lawyer of Gansu Xiehe Law Firm.

Respondent (Plaintiff at First Instance): Aksai Kazak Autonomous County Sub-branch of Agricultural Bank of China. Domicile: Aksai Kazak Autonomous County, Gansu Province.

Responsible Person: Li Yi, President of the Sub-branch.

Agent ad litem: Song Yingchun, cadre of the Legal Department of Agricultural Bank of China.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Ning, Deputy Director of Gansu Provincial Branch of Agricultural Bank of China.

The appellant Gansu Provincial Agricultural Reclamation General Company (hereinafter referred to as the Agricultural Reclamation General Company), for the dispute over guaranty for loan contract with the respondent Aksai Kazak Autonomous County Sub-branch of Agricultural Bank of China (hereinafter referred to as Aksai County Agricultural Bank), appealed against the civil judgment (1999) Gan Jing Chu Zi No. 29 rendered by Gansu High People's Court. This Court lawfully formed a collegial panel and conducted trial, which has now been concluded.

It is found that: From 1992 to March 1994, the An'nanba Asbestos Mine of Gansu Province (hereinafter referred to as the Asbestos Mine), a subordinate unit of the Agricultural Reclamation General Company, accumulated an overdue loan of RMB 2,755,000 from Aksai County Agricultural Bank. On March 22, 1994, the Agricultural Reclamation General Company entered into a loan guaranty agreement with Aksai County Agricultural Bank. The parties agreed that the Agricultural Reclamation General Company would provide a one-time guaranty for the loan of RMB 2,755,000 from the Bank owed by the Asbestos Mine. The term of the agreement was from the date of signing until the date when the borrowing party repays the loan principal and interest in full. Afterwards, on August 17, 1995, the Agricultural Reclamation General Company issued a letter to Aksai County Agricultural Bank titled "Letter on Providing Limited Guaranty for Bank Loans of the Asbestos Mine." The letter stated: "Given that the subordinate Asbestos Mine is far from Lanzhou, sporadic guaranties are time-sensitive and wasteful of time and effort, the Agricultural Reclamation General Company decides to provide a limited guaranty for the new round of loans between the Asbestos Mine and your bank. From the date hereof, the Company will provide a credit guaranty for the portion of cumulative loans within RMB 2,000,000. The above guaranty period is one year, calculated from the date of the loan." As of November 14, the Asbestos Mine borrowed 44 loans from Aksai County Agricultural Bank, totaling RMB 2,890,000. On July 20, 1996, Aksai County Agricultural Bank and the Asbestos Mine entered into a loan contract, agreeing that Aksai County Agricultural Bank would provide a working capital loan of RMB 500,000 at an interest rate of 10.65‰, with a loan period from July 20, 1996, to December 30, 1996. Among them, RMB 150,000 was lent on July 20, 1996, and RMB 350,000 on August 20, 1996. RMB 200,000 was due to be repaid on November 30, and RMB 300,000 on December 30. Aksai County Agricultural Bank disbursed RMB 150,000 to the Asbestos Mine on July 23, and RMB 200,000 on September 9, as agreed. On August 20 of the same year, Aksai County Agricultural Bank and the Asbestos Mine entered into a loan contract for RMB 2,890,000, stipulating a loan interest rate of 10.98‰, with a term of one year from August 20, 1996, to August 20, 1997. At the same time, on August 20, the Agricultural Reclamation General Company separately signed guaranty contracts with Aksai County Agricultural Bank for the above loans of RMB 500,000 and RMB 2,890,000, undertaking joint and several guaranty liability for the RMB 500,000 loan. In the guaranty contract for RMB 2,890,000, it was expressly stipulated that the guaranty period ends two years after the maturity of the loan, and if the borrower fails to repay the loan principal and interest on time, the guarantor shall bear joint and several guaranty liability and unconditionally repay the principal and interest on behalf of the borrower on time. On the day the loan contract was signed, Aksai County Agricultural Bank used a special transfer voucher to make an accounting adjustment, noting in the transfer reason column: "Transferred from Anying Office: 44 loans totaling RMB 2,890,000 from 1992 to 1995 of the Asbestos Mine, with a new loan contract signed and guaranty procedures completed by mutual agreement," and gave one copy of the special transfer voucher to the Asbestos Mine. On December 23 of the same year, the Asbestos Mine stamped and confirmed on the overdue loan and interest balance statement issued by Aksai County Agricultural Bank that as of December 20, 1996, the overdue loan was RMB 3,240,000 and overdue interest was RMB 416,785.02. During this period, Aksai County Agricultural Bank made a suspense entry of RMB 1,800,000 for the overdue interest of the Asbestos Mine. On August 11, 1998, the Asbestos Mine applied to the Aksai County People's Court for bankruptcy. Aksai County Agricultural Bank declared creditors' rights of principal of RMB 3,260,000 and interest of RMB 1,869,298.49 to the Aksai County Court in November. The Aksai County People's Court, by civil ruling (1999) A Jing Po Zi No. 1 on February 9, 1999, declared the Asbestos Mine bankrupt, with a zero repayment ratio for third-order creditors. On December 22 of the same year, Aksai County Agricultural Bank applied for a payment order for the principal of RMB 3,240,000 guaranteed by the Agricultural Reclamation General Company for the Asbestos Mine and interest of RMB 985,472.65. On January 15, 1999, the Agricultural Reclamation General Company filed a written objection to the payment order of the Aksai County People's Court, stating: "On July 23, 1996, August 20, 1996, and September 9, 1996, the Asbestos Mine, with the objector providing guaranty, borrowed RMB 150,000, RMB 2,890,000, and RMB 200,000 respectively from the objected party, totaling RMB 3,240,000. In addition, our company calculates the interest at RMB 434,289.26, which differs from the objected party's calculation of RMB 985,472.65 by RMB 551,183.39." Therefore, on April 28, 1999, Aksai County Agricultural Bank filed a lawsuit with Gansu High People's Court, requesting that Gansu Agricultural Reclamation General Company bear joint and several guaranty liability for the above loans.

It is further found that: During the first instance of this case, Gansu High People's Court on May 4, 1999, by civil ruling (1999) Gan Jing Chu Zi No. 29, froze RMB 4,467,900 in bank deposits of Gansu Agricultural Reclamation General Company.

Gansu High People's Court held after trial that: The loan contract between Aksai County Agricultural Bank and the Asbestos Mine was legally valid. The guaranty contracts and letters provided by the Agricultural Reclamation General Company for the loans of the Asbestos Mine and for continuous guaranty were also valid. The guaranty loan agreement, guaranty letter, guaranty loan contract signed between the Agricultural Reclamation General Company and Aksai County Agricultural Bank, and the objection to the payment order by the Agricultural Reclamation General Company to the Aksai County People's Court and other evidence all confirm that the loan contract for RMB 2,890,000 and the guaranty loan contract signed by the three parties on August 20, 1996, were a reconfirmation of the accumulated overdue loans of the Asbestos Mine in the past and represented the true intentions of the three parties. Therefore, Aksai County Agricultural Bank's claim that the Agricultural Reclamation General Company should bear guaranty liability for the principal and interest of RMB 2,890,000 was well-founded. As for the RMB 500,000 loan guaranteed by the Agricultural Reclamation General Company for the Asbestos Mine, since Aksai County Agricultural Bank actually disbursed only RMB 350,000, the Agricultural Reclamation General Company only bears guaranty liability for RMB 350,000. During the reform of the institutional system, after the Agricultural Reclamation General Company was restructured from the former Gansu Provincial Agricultural Reclamation Bureau into the Agricultural Reclamation General Company, it is no longer within the sequence of government agencies. Therefore, the Agricultural Reclamation General Company's argument that it did not meet the qualifications of a guarantor was unfounded. After discussion by the Judicial Committee, the Court, in accordance with Article 89, Paragraph 1, Item (1) of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 109 of the Supreme People's Court's Opinions on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the General Principles of the Civil Law, and Articles 6, 18, and 21, Paragraph 1 of the Guaranty Law of the People's Republic of China, decided: 1. The Agricultural Reclamation General Company shall repay Aksai County Agricultural Bank the loan principal of RMB 3,240,000 guaranteed for the Asbestos Mine and bear the interest within the loan period of RMB 416,706.35. 2. The Agricultural Reclamation General Company shall bear the overdue penalty for the above guaranteed loan of RMB 3,240,000 in the amount of RMB 903,292 (calculated at 4/10,000 per day. Among them, RMB 150,000, RMB 200,000, and RMB 2,890,000, respectively calculated from December 23, 1996, September 9, 1997, and August 20, 1997, until the effective date of this judgment). The case acceptance fee of RMB 32,350 and the preservation fee of RMB 22,340 shall be borne by the Agricultural Reclamation General Company.

The Agricultural Reclamation General Company, dissatisfied with the above civil judgment of Gansu High People's Court, appealed to this Court, stating: The loan contract for RMB 2,890,000 signed between Aksai County Agricultural Bank and the Asbestos Mine on August 20, 1996, was intended to help the Asbestos Mine resume production and operations and avoid bankruptcy. Aksai County Agricultural Bank, by fraudulent means, used the name of providing working capital loans to actually engage in a "new loan repaying old debt" scheme, causing the Asbestos Mine to sign the loan contract against its true intentions. According to relevant legal provisions, such conduct should be deemed invalid. If the loan contract is invalid, the guaranty contract as an ancillary contract also becomes invalid, and the Agricultural Reclamation General Company had no fault in this regard, thus it should not bear any liability. Even if the contract was valid, Aksai County Agricultural Bank's unauthorized use of a special transfer voucher after the contract was signed to apply the new loan to repay the old debt constituted a breach of contract, of which the guarantor Agricultural Reclamation General Company was unaware. Because Aksai County Agricultural Bank did not perform its loan obligation as agreed, the borrower naturally had no obligation to repay the loan. The guarantor's guaranty liability should therefore be exempted. The RMB 500,000 loan contract with the Asbestos Mine is an independent and valid contract, which is a different legal relationship from the RMB 2,890,000 loan involved in this case and should not be conflated. Aksai County Agricultural Bank only performed RMB 350,000, which constituted a breach of contract. This should be tried separately and decided accordingly. The appeal requested the reversal of the first-instance judgment and a ruling that the Agricultural Reclamation General Company does not bear guaranty liability for the principal and interest of the RMB 2,890,000 loan. Aksai County Agricultural Bank responded: The first-instance judgment found clear facts and applied the law accurately, requesting the affirmation of the original judgment and the dismissal of the Agricultural Reclamation General Company's appeal.

This Court holds: According to the facts mutually acknowledged by both parties, from 1992 to 1994, the Asbestos Mine borrowed from Aksai County Agricultural Bank a cumulative amount of RMB 2,890,000. On August 20, 1996, Aksai County Agricultural Bank separately signed a loan contract for RMB 2,890,000 and a guaranty contract with the Agricultural Reclamation General Company, with the loan amount identical to the previous cumulative overdue amount of the Asbestos Mine. After the contract was signed, Aksai County Agricultural Bank used a special transfer voucher to apply the new loan to repay the old debt and handed over the bank's accounting copy of the special transfer voucher, which indicated the reason for the transfer, to the Asbestos Mine, to which the Asbestos Mine raised no objection. Moreover, for more than two years thereafter, the Asbestos Mine did not raise any objection to Aksai County Agricultural Bank's failure to perform the loan disbursement obligation. The parties in this case had a common subjective intent to use a new loan to repay the old debt, and the contract's content did not violate current Chinese laws or administrative regulations, so it should be deemed legally valid. The Agricultural Reclamation General Company's appeal argument that Aksai County Agricultural Bank used fraudulent means to engage in a "new loan repaying old debt" under the guise of providing working capital loans, rendering the signed contract invalid, lacks factual basis and is not accepted by this Court. There was a long-standing lending relationship between Aksai County Agricultural Bank and the Asbestos Mine. Whether for the old loans in the past or for the new loan of RMB 2,890,000 signed in 1996, the Agricultural Reclamation General Company, as the superior supervisory unit of the borrower Asbestos Mine, provided guaranty through contracts or letters. Although Aksai County Agricultural Bank did not actually disburse the loan under the contract signed on August 20, 1996, that loan was used to repay the existing debt of the same amount guaranteed by the Agricultural Reclamation General Company, without increasing the guaranty liability of the Agricultural Reclamation General Company. Moreover, the Agricultural Reclamation General Company, as the superior supervisory unit of the Asbestos Mine, should have known the actual purpose of the Asbestos Mine's loan, and therefore should bear the corresponding guaranty liability. The Agricultural Reclamation General Company's appeal ground that it was unaware of the "new loan repaying old debt" and therefore refuses to bear guaranty liability cannot be established and is not supported by this Court. The loan contract for RMB 500,000 signed between Aksai County Agricultural Bank and the Asbestos Mine on July 20, 1996, had qualified parties, represented the true intentions of both parties, and its content did not violate laws or administrative regulations, so it should be deemed valid. Although after the contract was signed, Aksai County Agricultural Bank only disbursed RMB 350,000 for some reason, since the Asbestos Mine did not raise any objection for more than two years, it should be deemed that the Asbestos Mine had accepted this. For this loan contract, the Agricultural Reclamation General Company signed and stamped the guaranty contract on August 20, 1996, undertaking joint and several guaranty liability. According to Article 109 of the Supreme People's Court's Opinions on Several Issues Concerning the Implementation of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China (For Trial Implementation), which provides that "during the guaranty period, the guarantor's scope of guaranty may be reduced due to the reduction of the principal debt," the Agricultural Reclamation General Company shall still bear joint and several liability for repayment of the loan actually disbursed by Aksai County Agricultural Bank. Although the loan contract for RMB 500,000 signed between Aksai County Agricultural Bank and the Asbestos Mine on July 20, 1996, is an independent contract, given that the Asbestos Mine has already become bankrupt and the creditor's repayment ratio is zero, and the Agricultural Reclamation General Company did not raise any objection to the consolidated trial during the first instance, the first-instance court's consolidation of the trial was not improper. The Agricultural Reclamation General Company's appeal argument that the RMB 500,000 loan contract should be tried separately and that Aksai County Agricultural Bank was in breach of contract cannot be established and is not supported by this Court. The first-instance judgment found clear facts and applied the law correctly, and should generally be affirmed; however, given the general downward adjustment of loan interest rates by the People's Bank of China, the penalty interest rate of 4/10,000 per day ordered by the first-instance judgment for the Agricultural Reclamation General Company should be adjusted accordingly. This Court, in accordance with Article 153, Paragraph 1, Item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, hereby adjudges as follows:

1. Affirms Item 1 of the main text of the civil judgment (1999) Gan Jing Chu Zi No. 29 of Gansu High People's Court and the portion concerning the case acceptance fee and preservation fee.

2. Changes Item 2 of the main text of the civil judgment (1999) Gan Jing Chu Zi No. 29 of Gansu High People's Court to: Gansu Provincial Agricultural Reclamation General Company shall pay a late payment penalty of RMB 3,240,000 (calculated at the overdue loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China for the same period. Among them, RMB 150,000, RMB 200,000, and RMB 2,890,000, respectively calculated from December 23, 1996, September 9, 1997, and August 21, 1997, until the date of payment) to Aksai Kazak Autonomous County Sub-branch of Agricultural Bank of China.

The above amount shall be paid within ten days from the day following service of this judgment. If payment is overdue, the matter shall be handled in accordance with Article 232 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.

The second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 32,350 shall be borne by the appellant Gansu Provincial Agricultural Reclamation General Company.

This judgment is final.

Presiding Judge: Li Tianshun

Judge: Xu Ruibai

Acting Judge: Wang Tao

December 26, 1999

Clerk: Li Guohui
